title: No Peace Without Him
translation: As long as people do not worship the lotus feet of Uma's lord, in this world or the next, they find no happiness, no peace, no end to their suffering. Be pleased, O Lord, who dwells in all beings.
translation_hi: जब तक मनुष्य इस लोक या परलोक में उमापति के चरण कमलों का भजन नहीं करते, तब तक उन्हें न सुख मिलता है, न शांति, न दुःखों का नाश होता है। हे सब प्राणियों में निवास करने वाले प्रभु, प्रसन्न होइए।
grammar: Yavat … tavat: 'as long as … so long', like Hindi जब तक … तब तक.

Meter note: the scanner marks two syllables in line 1: यावद् उमा gives light-light where the meter wants heavy-light. Tulsidas's Sanskrit allows small freedoms like this; reciters simply lengthen the syllable.
Aravinda again: 'lotus', as in अरविन्दचक्षुस् (lotus-eyed) in Tandava verse 12.
